chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from some of our companions, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

Regarding the mud of rain: there is no harm in it touching the garment for three days, unless it is known that something made it impure after the rain. But if it touches it after three days, then wash it; and if the road is clean, then you do not wash it.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: if a person thinks that some impurity has reached his garment but is not certain of that, he should sprinkle it with water. If he is certain that impurity has occurred in it and knows its place, he should wash it with water. But if he does not know the exact place, he should wash the entire garment with water so that he may be certain of its purity and that doubt and uncertainty may be removed from him regarding it.

The basis in this matter is that when impurity occurs in a garment, salat in it becomes forbidden. If he does not know the exact place and then washes it, he becomes certain of the garment’s purity. Whenever the place is not specifically known to him, there is no way for him to judge the garment to be pure except after washing all of it; and this is also indicated by the evidence.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing under discussion
key_terms.الشَّكُّ: doubt regarding whether impurity is present
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity depends here on purity of clothing
key_terms.رَشَّهُ: he sprinkled it, meaning to apply water when impurity is only suspected
key_terms.طِينِ الْمَطَرِ: mud formed by rainwater, discussed here in relation to purity
key_terms.نَجَاسَةٌ: ritual impurity affecting the validity of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on rain mud or suspected impurity on clothing before salat?
ai.summary: This report discusses rulings of ritual purity concerning rain mud and impurity on garments. It explains when contact with mud does not require washing, and it sets out the principle that certainty of impurity in clothing prevents salat in it until the impurity is removed with certainty.
